newsitem.title: VIETNAM: U.S. election over, Vietnam sneers at Clinton.
newsitem.headline: U.S. election over, Vietnam sneers at Clinton.

text.p: Vietnam launched a sneering attack on U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday, just days after welcoming his re-election as the world's most powerful man.
Newspapers, radio and television broadcast a lengthy commentary questioning the achievements of his first term in office and his moral authority to lead the United States.
"Significantly, the strategy that 'being re-elected is most important' has deformed many of B. Clinton's principles and policies," the commentary said.
"...he has turned the results of a period of (cyclical) economic recovery into his own merits," it added.
Hanoi's relations with Washington have blown from lukewarm to frosty since the two normalised diplomatic ties in July 1995, capping two decades of formal animosity dating back to the Vietnam War.
Diplomats from both countries maintain that relations are progressing gradually but well despite slow progress towards full economic and trade normalisation.

Vietnam was among the first Asian countries to welcome Clinton's re-election earlier this week -- a result which some observers say came as a relief to those in Hanoi concerned about tough statements on Vietnam by Republican candidate Bob Dole.
But behind the diplomatic politesse it has shown a more cautious regard for its former foe.
Regular commentaries in the official press have slammed U.S. policy over issues from Cuba to the launching of U.S. radio station Asia Pacific Network, formerly Radio Free Asia.
Senior officials have also warned of elements within the United States seeking to undermine Hanoi's socialist system through a process of 'peaceful evolution'.
